title: Texas Widens H-1B Fraud Probe, Targets Nearly 30 'Ghost Office' Firms
excerpt: Attorney General Ken Paxton's investigation into sham H-1B operations has expanded from three companies to nearly 30, with federal agencies now facing pressure to launch their own probe.
body:
• Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has issued civil investigative demands to nearly 30 North Texas businesses suspected of H-1B visa fraud through "ghost offices."
  • The investigation, which began in January 2026 targeting three firms, has expanded to include companies such as Tekpro IT, Blooming Clouds, and Virat Solutions.
  • Governor Abbott froze all new H-1B petitions for state agencies and universities through May 2027, while a legislative committee is probing the program's oversight.
  • Congressional representatives from Texas have called on DHS, the State Department, and the Department of Labor for a coordinated federal investigation.

Texas has dramatically expanded its crackdown on alleged H-1B visa fraud, with Attorney General Ken Paxton issuing civil investigative demands to nearly 30 North Texas businesses suspected of exploiting the program through sham operations — a probe that carries significant implications for the Indian IT workforce that relies heavily on H-1B sponsorships.

The 'Ghost Office' Scheme

At the center of the investigation are so-called "ghost offices" — businesses that authorities allege set up fake operations in Texas to sponsor foreign workers under the H-1B program. According to Paxton's office, some of the firms registered single-family homes as corporate addresses or listed empty, unfinished buildings as worksites, with no evidence of actual business operations, products, or services at those locations.

"I will not allow the H-1B program to be abused by bad actors seeking to use it as a loophole for allowing foreign nationals to invade Texas."

— Ken Paxton, Texas Attorney General

The companies under scrutiny include Tekpro IT LLC, Fame PBX LLC, 1st Ranking Technologies LLC, Qubitz Tech Systems LLC, Blooming Clouds LLC, Virat Solutions Inc., Oak Technologies Inc., Techpath Inc., and Techquency LLC, among others. Paxton's office has demanded employee rosters, financial statements, records of products and services, and internal communications from each firm.

From Three Firms to Thirty

The investigation traces back to January 2026, when reports of fraudulent H-1B sponsorships by businesses with little or no commercial activity first surfaced in North Texas. Paxton initially targeted three companies. The probe has since ballooned, with each round of demands uncovering additional entities suspected of similar schemes.

Governor Greg Abbott moved in parallel, directing all Texas state agencies and universities to freeze new H-1B visa petitions and launch a review of current program use. That freeze remains in effect through May 2027.

"The economy of Texas should work for the benefit of Texas workers and Texas employers," Abbott said in his directive. "State government must lead by example and ensure that employment opportunities — particularly those funded with taxpayer dollars — are filled by Texans first."

Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows has also directed a legislative committee to investigate whether the state has sufficient visibility into employer use of the H-1B program to identify patterns that affect the Texas workforce or raise security concerns.

Federal Pressure Builds

The Texas investigations have triggered action at the federal level. Representative Beth Van Duyne and several other Texas House members wrote to Trump administration officials calling for a coordinated, interagency investigation involving the Department of Homeland Security, the State Department, and the Department of Labor.

Their letter called for a review of H-1B adjudication processes, strengthened enforcement with increased audits, improved data sharing between agencies, and recommendations to Congress on statutory changes to close loopholes.

Separately, the DOL has launched Project Firewall, an enforcement initiative focused on wage violations and misrepresentation of working conditions in H-1B sponsorships. Congress is also considering the bipartisan H-1B and L-1 Visa Reform Act of 2025, which proposes stricter wage baselines and expanded compliance tools.

Impact on Indian IT Workers

While the investigations target employers rather than visa holders, the fallout could ripple through the Indian IT community. Indian nationals hold the majority of H-1B visas, and many work through staffing and consulting firms — the very model now under scrutiny.

Legal experts note that Texas' enforcement approach rests on state consumer-protection law rather than immigration authority, which remains federal. But the political momentum could influence H-1B enforcement nationwide, as other state attorneys general have access to similar consumer-protection statutes.

Workers employed by firms under investigation face potential disruption to their immigration status if their employer's petitions are revoked. Immigration attorneys advise affected H-1B holders to review their employment documentation, confirm their worksite arrangements match their petition filings, and consult legal counsel if their employer is named in any investigation.
